observations.title: Trading Glossary — Every Term Explained | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A complete plain-language trading glossary, browsable by category, with practice on the free $100,000 simulator. Educational only.

observations.title: Backtesting — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Testing a strategy against historical data to evaluate its hypothetical performance.

observations.title: Bear Trap — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A bear trap is a false breakdown below support that tricks traders into short positions before price reverses upward, squeezing shorts as it rallies.

observations.title: Bollinger Band Squeeze — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A Bollinger Band squeeze describes a narrow distance between the bands relative to a selected comparison period.

observations.title: Bull Trap — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A bull trap is a false breakout above resistance that lures buyers into long positions before price reverses sharply downward, trapping them with losses.

observations.title: Candlestick Patterns — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Candlestick patterns are names for formations built from opening, high, low and closing prices.

observations.title: Circuit Breaker — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A rule-defined trading pause.

observations.title: Correlation Trading — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Studying sampled relationships between asset returns.

observations.title: Dark Pool — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A non-displayed trading venue where orders generally do not appear in public pre-trade quotes.

observations.title: Day Trading — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Day trading means opening and closing positions within a trading day.

observations.title: Death Cross — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A death cross is the bearish counterpart to the golden cross.

observations.title: Dollar Cost Averaging — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Dollar-cost averaging means contributing fixed amounts at regular intervals regardless of price.

observations.title: Double Bottom — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A double bottom is a W-shaped chart pattern with two troughs near a similar level.

observations.title: Drawdown — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The decline from a portfolio's peak value to its lowest point before a new peak.

observations.title: Elliott Wave Theory — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Elliott wave theory interprets price patterns using impulse and corrective wave counts.

observations.title: Fair Value Gap (FVG) — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A Fair Value Gap is a three-candle chart pattern where the wicks of the first and third candles do not overlap.

observations.title: Fibonacci Retracement — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Fibonacci retracement is a technical analysis tool using horizontal lines at key ratios (23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%) to indicate potential support and resistance levels.

observations.title: Flash Crash — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: An extremely rapid and deep market decline followed by a swift recovery, typically lasting minutes.

observations.title: FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: FOMO is the anxiety-driven urge to trade because a price is moving or others appear to be profiting.

observations.title: FUD (Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt) — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Negative information — true, exaggerated, or fabricated — spread to create panic and drive prices down.

observations.title: Golden Cross — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A golden cross is a bullish technical signal that occurs when a short-term moving average (typically the 50-day) crosses above a long-term moving average (typically the 200-day).

observations.title: Head and Shoulders — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A head and shoulders pattern has three peaks, with a higher central peak and two lower shoulders.

observations.title: HODL Strategy — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: HODL is a buy-and-hold expression associated with a Bitcoin forum typo.

observations.title: Ichimoku Cloud — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A comprehensive Japanese indicator system showing support/resistance, trend direction, and momentum in a single view.

observations.title: Impermanent Loss — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The opportunity cost of providing liquidity in a DEX pool compared to simply holding the assets.

observations.title: Leverage Trading — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Control a larger market position with borrowed funds or margin.

observations.title: Limit Order vs Market Order — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Market orders seek prompt execution at available prices.

observations.title: Liquidation Cascade — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A liquidation cascade is feedback in which forced position reductions add price pressure that can trigger further reductions.

observations.title: Liquidation Price — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A liquidation price is an estimate of the level at which a leveraged position may be closed under a platform's margin rules.

observations.title: Moving Average Convergence Divergence — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: MACD shows the relationship between two EMAs.

observations.title: MACD Histogram — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line as vertical bars.

observations.title: Margin Call — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A broker's demand for additional collateral when your account equity falls below the maintenance margin requirement.

observations.title: Market Maker — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A market maker posts bid and ask quotes under venue rules to facilitate trading.

observations.title: Order Block — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: An order block is a chart-defined zone used in some technical-analysis frameworks; candles alone do not establish actual institutional orders.

observations.title: Paper Trading — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Simulated trading with virtual money to study order mechanics and compare ideas.

observations.title: Pump and Dump — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A fraud scheme where promoters artificially inflate an asset's price through misleading hype, then sell their holdings at the peak, crashing the price.

observations.title: Risk-Reward Ratio — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The risk-reward ratio compares a trade's planned loss with its planned gain.

observations.title: RSI Divergence — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: RSI divergence occurs when the Relative Strength Index moves opposite to price, signaling weakening momentum and potential reversal.

observations.title: Satoshi Nakamoto — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonym used by the creator of Bitcoin, who published its whitepaper in 2008.

observations.title: Scalping — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Scalping describes attempts to capture small price movements over short holding periods.

observations.title: Short Squeeze — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A short squeeze occurs when a rising price or difficulty borrowing a security puts pressure on short sellers to close positions by buying shares.

observations.title: Slippage — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The difference between expected trade price and actual execution price.

observations.title: Stop Loss Hunting — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: A suspected intentional move through levels where stop orders may be placed.

observations.title: Support and Resistance — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Support and resistance are price areas where traders look for repeated buying or selling responses.

observations.title: Swing Trading — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Holding positions for days to weeks to capture medium-term price swings.

observations.title: Volume Profile — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Shows trading volume distribution at each price level rather than over time.

observations.title: VWAP — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: VWAP is the average observed trading price weighted by volume over a stated period.

observations.title: Whale Manipulation — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Whale manipulation refers to large traders using substantial capital to artificially influence prices through spoofing, wash trading, and strategic order placement.

observations.title: Wyckoff Method — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: The Wyckoff method interprets price and volume through phases such as accumulation, markup, distribution and markdown.

observations.title: Yield Farming — Definition, Example & How to Trade It | TradeHQ Wiki
descriptions: Depositing crypto assets into DeFi protocols to earn rewards through trading fees, token incentives, or interest.
